summary: This article explains how skeletal muscles pull on bones in opposing pairs to create movement, and how exercise and rest make muscles stronger.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Muscles: How Your Body Moves” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a thin, thread-like strand that makes up part of a material
a place in the body where two bones meet and can move

challengeTerms.def: relating to the bones and the muscles that move them
a muscle that works opposite another muscle, relaxing when its partner contracts
the growth and thickening of muscle fibers after repeated exercise

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that muscles can push bones as well as pull them? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Write advice for a younger student about how to keep muscles strong and healthy.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review contract, fiber, and joint, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses skeletal, antagonist, and hypertrophy to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
